g1.label: 1 — a student ___ (not see) since Thursday
g1.why: “Since Thursday morning” reaches up to now, so use the present perfect passive: has/have + been + past participle.

g2.label: 2 — his mobile phone ___ (find)
g2.why: “On Friday morning” is a finished past time, so the simple past passive is right: was + found.

g3.label: 3 — his parents ___ (inform)
g3.why: No past time is given and the news still matters now, so the present perfect passive fits.

g4.label: 4 — a search ___ (call off) at sunset
g4.why: The report is written after sunset, so calling the search off is already over: simple past passive.

g5.label: 5 — many tourists ___ (attract) by bushwalking
g5.why: This is generally true, not a single event, so use the simple present passive.

g6.label: 6 — Jessica Harris ___ (find)
g6.why: “Last month” is a finished past time, so the simple past passive is needed.

g7.label: 7 — unless you ___ (give) survival training
g7.why: The training happens before the trip and leads up to it, so the present perfect passive fits.

g1.label: 1 — He ___ since.
g1.why: The active is present perfect (has seen), so the passive is has been seen — here in the negative.

g2.label: 2 — Jim ___ by that guy at the hostel
g2.why: The active is simple past (warned), so the passive is was + warned, and the doer follows with “by”.

g3.label: 3 — He ___ by somebody else
g3.why: The active is simple past (told). Jim receives the information, so he becomes the subject of was told.

g4.label: 4 — This guy ___.
g4.why: After will the passive is be + past participle: will be rescued.

g5.correct: isn't going to be called off
accept: isn't going to be called off
is not going to be called off
g5.label: 5 — The search ___ before they find him
g5.why: With going to, the passive is going to be + past participle; the negative stays on the form of be.

g6.label: 6 — He ___ by a snake
g6.why: The active is a simple past negative (didn’t bite), so the passive is wasn’t + bitten.

g7.label: 7 — He ___.
g7.why: After will the passive is be + past participle: will be found.

g1.label: 1 — would like ___ a room with a harbour view
g1.why: After would like the passive infinitive is to be + past participle. The guests receive the room, so: to be given.

g2.label: 2 — expect ___ to a barbie
g2.why: Expect takes the full infinitive, so the passive is to be taken, not just be taken.

g3.label: 3 — want ___ breakfast on the terrace
g3.why: The guests receive the breakfast, so want takes the passive infinitive to be served.

g4.label: 4 — would like ___ more information
g4.why: They receive the information, so the passive infinitive after would like is to be given.

g5.label: 5 — want ___ up for their flight
g5.why: The past participle of wake is woken, so the passive infinitive is to be woken; “up” is already in the sentence.

g6.label: 6 — hopes ___ about any parties
g6.why: He receives the information, so hope takes the passive infinitive to be told.
